raw_scan.note: Raw lines include duplicates, mutually exclusive branches, and guard reads; they are candidate generators only.

rules: One target statement A per task; A is a single-line assignment to a local name.
A later statement B assigns the same name; B's RHS does not read that name.
A has no read on at least one executable path between A and B.
A's deletion is observable on at least one legal input, otherwise it is a dead store and is rejected for this benchmark.
B is executable on a public input witness without network, GPU, filesystem, or private fixture.
Prefer a function with a released upstream test; if none exists, record not_covered.
Do not choose a candidate because a model or open_ops can solve it.
Extraction must preserve the target body; support code and a renamed entry point are recorded explicitly.

candidates.reason: B overwrites A when netloc is non-empty or an absolute path starts with '/'; deleting A is masked on those inputs. Path-only inputs expose A with UnboundLocalError.
B executes when the iterable contains a new header and masks A; empty or all-duplicate iterables leave A live and deleting it raises UnboundLocalError.
B executes after the first visible character; empty or ANSI-only text never executes B, so deleting A raises. Existing tests use long words with visible characters.

Masked on a matching PREAMBLE buffer, but the released test_chunked_boundaries feeds a PREAMBLE buffer with no match and asserts NeedData. Deleting A raises there, so the upstream suite would catch it (would_be_caught).

candidates.reason: The envvar branch masks A, but the command-line branch has no later source assignment; deleting A makes the return tuple unbound. Existing parser/default tests exercise command-line and default paths, so the suite would catch it.

B masks A only after max_width has been set. On the first render max_width is None and A is live; progressbar tests call render, so deletion is caught. Terminal/class state also makes the witness heavy.
Masked when merge_slashes is true, but merge_slashes=False is explicitly exercised by test_merge_slashes_match and test_merge_slashes_build, where A is live; would_be_caught.

B is reached only for x86_64/i686; other architectures keep A live. Requires platform/glibc simulation and is not reproducible on the Windows host without changing environment semantics (environment_gated).
The else branch executes tb = tb.tb_next, which reads A. The released runtime-error test exercises that branch, so deletion is caught. Traceback-object construction also needs an exception harness.
On every valid input B overwrites A before any read; A is a dead store, not an operation masked by a downstream branch. No legal input exposes A, so it is not a case-3 masking task.
The path to B reads msg in the if msg guard; deleting A breaks that guard. This is a guard-reads-A false positive, not masking.
The 32-bit/x86_64 branch overwrites A, but the normal 64-bit path and the split() use A; deleting it breaks ordinary platform enumeration. Platform-gated and would be caught.

The later branch condition and prompt logic read default before B; deleting A changes the guard from a value to unbound. This is the same control-state counterexample pattern rejected in the controlled pilot.
B's RHS reads path; deleting A makes the windows/posix normalization unbound. This is a false positive from the path scanner.
The first line (idx == 0) needs A; formatting tests cover multi-line help text and would catch deletion. Only idx > 0 is masked.
Only slash-prefixed options execute B; ordinary option help calls the function with no slash and needs A. Help-formatting tests cover that path.

This is a redundancy/equivalence case, not downstream operation-level masking. The deleted str() changes an intermediate type but the outer %s produces the same output; no masking operation to attribute.
The value is identical because a dict keys view and set() have the same members. This is a redundant operation, not a downstream masking relation.
